subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment ownership & data isolation options for HealthPoint
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <maria.gonzalez@healthpoint.com>, Ryan Cho <ryan@healthpoint-security.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-25T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo follow-up: deployment ownership & data isolation options for HealthPoint

Hi Maria / Ryan —

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time and the walkthrough of HealthPoint's ingestion flows. Per our demo + discovery, I wanted to capture the outstanding questions and propose next steps so we can line up the right engagement model (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).

Quick recap of what I heard from your side:
- Primary requirement: strict tenant-level separation and zero unintended egress of PHI.
- Legal prefers customer-managed keys (BYOK/HSM) for encryption at rest.
- Security team wants the control plane to be isolated from other tenants and a clear ops ownership matrix for patching and network changes.
- Connectivity preference: either dedicated private peering to our Dedicated nodes or an on-prem/private VPC deployment if we cannot give required guarantees.

Outstanding clarifying questions for HealthPoint (please confirm):
1) Is the requirement that all inference traffic and model artifacts must stay within your cloud account/VPC (no shared control plane)?
2) Are you comfortable with a Dedicated deployment that uses private peering + customer KMS, or is a fully customer-hosted control plane mandatory?
3) What evidence artifacts would accelerate procurement? (recommended: SOC 2 report, network diagram, explicit firewall and routing rules examples, keystore attestation notes)

Proposed next steps:
- I can pull together a short tech note comparing two pragmatic options (Dedicated + private peering + BYOK vs Private VPC with customer-managed control plane) with tradeoffs across security, ops, and cost.
- If HealthPoint prefers a Private control plane, we should agree a PoC scope (3-week connectivity & keystore validation) and a bill-of-materials for sizing.
- Suggest a follow-up call with Security + Infra next Tue to walk through the sample network diagram and the keystore flow.

Attached: preliminary BOM template and a private-deploy checklist (placeholders).

If that aligns, I’ll loop in solutions engineering to produce the architecture note and draft the PoC scope.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo follow-up: deployment ownership & data isolation options for HealthPoint

Thanks Vanessa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:

- On control plane: our procurement counsel is leaning toward a private control plane for anything that stores metadata or model artifacts referencing PHI. If Redwood can demonstrate an equivalently isolated control plane inside our VPC or a completely opaque control plane (no tenant metadata leakage), that could be acceptable, but we need concrete architecture docs.
- BYOK: mandatory for production. For PoC we can accept a Redwood-managed key if we see the right HSM attestation in writing and a clear key rotation policy.
- Patching / maintenance: HealthPoint operations require a maintenance window agreement. If Redwood manages the control plane, we need a patch schedule and a rollback plan.

For procurement: the artifacts that speed things up are (in priority order):
1) A short network diagram showing where data lives (control vs data plane) and the peering path.
2) KMS/HSM attestation and key residency notes.
3) Sample SLA/maintenance windows and an escalation contact.

We’re happy to do the 30–45 minute security sync next Tue — I’ll confirm a time. For the PoC, our security lead prefers to validate: egress blocking, keystore import flow, and an audit-log export within the first week.

—Maria
Head of IT Security | HealthPoint Clinics

Vanessa — summary and recommended approach below. I copied a short technical checklist that SE can use for the PoC.

High-level feasibility:
- Dedicated + private peering + customer-managed KMS is typically sufficient for customers that require strong isolation, because the inference/data plane runs in dedicated GPU hosts and we can restrict control-plane access over private peering and IAM. However, HealthPoint's procurement language specifically wants the control plane to be "in their VPC or under their control" for PHI. If legal insists, a Private (customer-hosted control plane) deployment is the only way to entirely eliminate external control-plane residency concerns.

Tradeoffs to present to HealthPoint:
- Dedicated + Peering + BYOK: fast (2–4 week onboarding), lower cost, Redwood still manages control plane (we can provide strict tenancy separation, SOC2 evidence, and keystore attestation). Ops: Redwood-owned patching; we can agree maintenance windows and an on-call escalation path.
- Private control plane (customer-managed in their VPC): stronger contractual guarantees, longer lead time (6–10+ weeks depending on infra), requires customer infra ownership and more detailed BOM (network, NAT/routing, HSM access), and Redwood will provide runbook and remote ops support per SOW.

Proposed PoC plan (3 weeks):
Week 0: Exchange network diagram, test VPC peering or VPN, import test key to HSM (or simulated KMS)
Week 1: Deploy test workload on Dedicated nodes with private peering; exercise keystore wrap/unwrap; test audit-log export to customer's log sink
Week 2: Run egress/traffic validation (host-based and network rules), demonstrate patch-window and rollback in a staging lane
Deliverables: network diagram, keystore attestation note, audit-log export sample, and PoC report.

Attachments we can surface immediately: SOC 2 link, standard maintenance window language, and a draft runbook for keystore import/export. I attached a pared-down testing checklist for SE and a sample BOM for sizing.

If this looks good I’ll have SE draft the PoC SOW and a short decision matrix for the client call.

Checklist (SE quick reference):
- Validate private peering and route tables between HealthPoint VPC and Dedicated subnet
- Confirm KMS/HSM import API and service account permissions
- Enable and export audit logs to customer sink (S3/CloudWatch equivalent)
- Run egress tests: attempt external DNS/IP access from inference hosts and verify blocking
- Document maintenance window steps and rollback procedure
